answer: A concrete sybil defence is a slow admission inlet: a newcomer enters with almost no rights and must anchor its identity to a long-lived, verifiable record of useful work before it can act. Each agent emits a steady pulse of signed activity that peers can check, so a fresh identity with no history cannot fake standing overnight. An attacker can mint a thousand names, but none carries the anchored history or the regular pulse of real work, so they all stay locked at the inlet while honest agents pass.
